Name: Alex's Snow Accumulation
Author: xBrince
Description:
[center][size=6][b]Alex's Snow Accumulation[/b][/size]
[i]Snow that builds up on the floors you place.[/i][/center]

[b]BETA (v0.11.0).[/b] Snow on floors, the Snow Shovel, the crunch sounds and the snow edges have all been played in the game. Tractor Mod support, the experimental Snow Everywhere mode and multiplayer have barely or never been tried (details further down). Back up your saves before trying a beta, and tell me what you find.

[b]Made with AI.[/b] All of the code and artwork, and the text of this page, were produced with AI (Claude, by Anthropic). The footstep recording, from Pixabay, appears to be AI-generated too. See "Credits and AI disclosure" at the bottom.

[line]

[size=4][b]What it does[/b][/size]
In winter, the floors and paths you place (wood floor, stone floor, cobblestone path, gravel, stepping stones and so on, including other mods' floors) collect snow while it snows, instead of staying spotless. The snow gets deeper the longer it snows, melts away on dry winter days, and you clear it with your hoe or the new Snow Shovel, which pushes it off the path into snow piles. Walking on it crunches.

[size=4][b]Four snow depths[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][b]Bare[/b] - no snow, but in winter the floor gets a light dusting so it never looks spotless.[/*]
[*][b]Powder[/b] - a thin, flat layer with soft, feathered edges.[/*]
[*][b]Coated[/b] - real, raised snow with a soft edge and a shadow.[/*]
[*][b]Covered[/b] - a second raised layer on top, so it reads as clearly deeper. Next to coated snow it forms a step.[/*]
[/list]Snow keeps deepening while it keeps snowing. With the default settings the first layer is down after 4 hours of snow, and each further layer takes another 6, so a full day of snow goes roughly: coated everywhere by hour 4, covered on about half the floor by hour 7, covered everywhere by hour 10. If you prefer, switch to "overnight" mode: snowy mornings simply start with everything outdoors covered. A thaw takes tiles down one level at a time. You can cap the deepest snow at powder, coated or covered.

[size=4][b]Natural edges[/b][/size]
Snow does not stop on the tile lines like a ruler. Where deep snow meets bare floor its edge is a little rough and rounded, and where the thin powder meets bare floor it thins out into a feathered, drifting edge with a few flakes blown past the border. A single bare tile in a snowfield looks like a hole with a curved edge; a one-tile path or pier keeps a solid line of snow down its middle. Where two snowy tiles meet there is no seam. There is a "Snow edge roughness" setting: Off (the old straight edges), Gentle, Medium (default) or Strong.

[size=4][b]Clearing snow[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][b]The hoe[/b] clears snow from a floor tile (the whole tile, or one level per swing if you prefer). The cleared snow is pushed off the path onto open ground as a snow pile. Piles beside each other join into long banks, with corners and junctions. A pickaxe or axe breaks a pile up again, and piles melt a little each dry winter day.[/*]
[*][b]The Snow Shovel[/b] is a tool that does one job: it moves snow. One click clears a straight line of tiles in front of you (3 by default, 1 to 5 in the settings) and it NEVER tills the ground, digs up artifact spots or cuts weeds. Clint sells it for 500g (the price, or the shop line, can be changed or turned off), or type snow_shovel in the SMAPI console. It costs what a hoe swing costs in stamina, or nothing if you change that setting.[/*]
[*]Snow on props joined to a cleared tile (string-light posts, benches, snowmen...) is cleared with it.[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]Crunchy footsteps[/b][/size]
Walking on snow (or through a pile) replaces the footstep sound with a snow crunch. There are eight different steps, picked at random but never one of the last three, so it does not sound like a loop. By default only raised snow crunches (powder stays quiet); you can change that. The crunch has its own volume slider (default 70%) on top of the game's Footstep volume, and 0% turns it off. Tiles without snow and tiles you have cleared keep their normal sound.

[size=4][b]Settings[/b][/size]
Everything is adjustable in Generic Mod Config Menu (page "Snow Accumulation"), or in config.json: how snow builds up (gradually (minor frame skipping on time ticks esp if you enable snow everywhere, not very imposing), or overnight (shouldnt have any performance impact)), how deep it gets and how fast, how much melts, what the hoe and shovel do, how far snow is flung, whether piles join, slow-down when walking on snow (off by default), sound settings, edge roughness, the winter dusting, and more. Generic Mod Config Menu is optional; without it you can edit config.json.

[size=4][b]Works with Tractor Mod (optional, recommended if you make the snow more of an obstacle)[/b][/size]
If you have Pathoschild's Tractor Mod, its hoe clears the snow around the tractor the way your own hoe does, and its pickaxe and axe break up snow piles. With the Snow Shovel selected, the tractor clears snow and never tills, which fixes "the tractor chops up the ground". [b]Note:[/b] this has been checked against the Tractor Mod 4.24.4. If a Tractor Mod update changes the parts this mod hooks into, the mod logs a warning and the tractor carries on as it always did.

[size=4][b]EXPERIMENTAL: Snow Everywhere (off by default)[/b][/size]
A switch in the settings that puts snow on the map's own ground too (grass, dirt, sand, roads, plazas, boardwalks) in every outdoor location in winter. It is [b]highly untested[/b]: it reaches into drawing, the hoe, the weather and your save file, and nobody has played it for long. If you try it, back up your saves first. With it off (the default) the mod does not even install the extra game hooks it needs.

[size=4][b]Requirements[/b][/size]
[list]
[*]Stardew Valley 1.6 and [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/2400]SMAPI[/url] 4.0.0 or newer (made and played on game 1.6.15 and SMAPI 4.5.2). Content Patcher is not needed.[/*]
[*]Optional: [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]Generic Mod Config Menu[/url] (settings page) and [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/1401]Tractor Mod[/url] (tractor support).[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]Install, update, uninstall[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][b]Install:[/b] unzip so you end up with Mods\SnowAccumulation. It is safe to add to an existing save. It only does anything in winter (and in other seasons only if you turn on "show outside winter", which is for testing).[/*]
[*][b]Update:[/b] replace the whole SnowAccumulation folder. Your config.json stays; new settings take their defaults.[/*]
[*][b]Uninstall:[/b] BEFORE removing the mod, load your save, type [b]snow_clear all[/b] in the SMAPI console and save. Snow piles are real objects in your save, and without the mod the game would show them as Error Items. A Snow Shovel you own also turns into an Error Item (it still swings like a hoe): put it in a chest first so it is easy to find. Everything melts at the end of winter anyway, so removing the mod in spring or summer leaves no piles. Snow depth itself needs no cleanup.[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]Try it without waiting for winter[/b][/size]
Type [b]snow_fall[/b] in the SMAPI console to pretend four hours of snow have fallen where you are (again to deepen it). Outside winter, type [b]snow_force on[/b] first.

[size=4][b]Compatibility and known limits[/b][/size]
[list]
[*]Snow is only drawn outdoors (not in the greenhouse) and only in winter. Only floors you place get snow, unless you switch on Snow Everywhere.[/*]
[*]Single-player only so far; multiplayer is untested.[/*]
[*]The dusting and powder are drawn over floors that other mods retexture as well, but they do not follow those floors' tile patterns, so they can look a little different there.[/*]
[*]The winter dusting on bare floor is still one repeating picture per tile, and a few of its pieces show a small clump cut off at the tile edge.[/*]
[*]A pickaxe or axe on the floor itself still removes the floor, as it always did. Only the hoe, the Snow Shovel (and the tractor's hoe) clear snow.[/*]
[*]A map can opt out of ground snow with the map property Alex.SnowAccumulation/NoSnow. Festivals are skipped.[/*]
[*]If one of the mod's game hooks ever fails, it logs a single line in the SMAPI log and the game's own code carries on.[/*]
[*]The snow is drawn in cached pictures, one per block of 8 x 8 tiles, and only repainted when the snow around that block changes (a few thousandths of a second per block, at most 3 blocks per frame), so a big change spreads over a few frames. If anything goes wrong there, it falls back to the old tile-by-tile drawing.[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]Bug reports[/b][/size]
Please post your SMAPI log (upload it at [url=https://smapi.io/log]smapi.io/log[/url] and paste the link), the version you use (0.11.0), and what you were doing. Screenshots help, and for anything about edges that look odd, please say which zoom level you use.

[spoiler]
[list]
[*]snow_fall [hours] - pretend it has snowed this many hours here (default 4)[/*]
[*]snow_cover [radius] [depth] - put snow on floors at once (depth 1 powder, 2 coated, 3 covered)[/*]
[*]snow_clear [all] - clear snow and remove snow piles (this location, or everywhere)[/*]
[*]snow_force on|off - show snow in any season (testing)[/*]
[*]snow_edges [off|gentle|medium|strong] - show or change how rough the snow edges are[/*]
[*]snow_crunch - play one crunch at the current volume[/*]
[*]snow_shovel - put a Snow Shovel in your pack[/*]
[*]snow_everywhere on|off, snow_ground - the experimental mode[/*]
[*]snow_trace on|off - log every hoe swing on a floor tile (debugging)[/*]
[/list][/spoiler]

[spoiler]
Snow depth is one number in each floor's own mod data, so it is saved with your game and goes away if you pick the floor up. The raised snow and the powder are painted into one picture per block of 8 x 8 tiles from the tile map and each pixel's position in the world, so neighbouring blocks always fit and nothing flickers. The shovel is a game tool of the "Hoe" kind with its own name and picture; the game only lets mods add tools of its own kinds. The full technical notes are in the README inside the download.[/spoiler]

[*][b]Footstep sounds:[/b] a recording from Pixabay by user FreeEverythingxx (it appears to be AI-generated), cut into eight steps, level-matched, faded in and out to avoid clicks and converted to mono WAV. Used under the Pixabay Content License, which allows free use and modification into new works.[/*]
[*][b]Tools:[/b] SMAPI by Pathoschild (including the Harmony library it ships with). Optional: Generic Mod Config Menu by spacechase0 and Tractor Mod by Pathoschild. None of their code is included.[/*]
[*]Permission: you are welcome to build on this mod or use parts of it in your own mods with credit (see the permissions on this page; the footstep sounds stay under their own licence).[/*]
[/list]

Manifest.Name: Alex's Snow Accumulation
Manifest.Description: Placed floors and paths collect snow in four depths while it snows (gradually, deepening as it keeps snowing, or overnight), a hoe (or the new Snow Shovel tool, sold at Clint's, which clears a line of tiles in one click and never tills) shovels it off the path into snow piles that join into banks and that a pickaxe or axe breaks up, bare floors get a light winter dusting, and walking on snow crunches (its own volume slider), and snow has natural, rounded, feathered edges instead of ruler-straight tile borders (adjustable). Works with Pathoschild's Tractor Mod if you have it (a selected Snow Shovel makes the tractor clear snow without tilling). Settings are in Generic Mod Config Menu, including an experimental, off-by-default mode that puts snow on the map's own ground everywhere. Made with AI (Claude by Anthropic): all code and data are AI-generated, and the footstep recording (from Pixabay, user FreeEverythingxx) appears to be AI-generated too.
